desc: On 27 September 2010 Robert Hastings convened seven United States Air Force veterans at the National Press Club in Washington DC to describe unidentified aerial incursions at nuclear weapons sites during the Cold War, including missile malfunctions occurring moments after disc-shaped craft were observed near underground launch silos. CNN streamed the event live. This is the pivot event for the whole nuclear strand and the reason this board grades that strand higher than the crash-retrieval literature it sits beside: it converted anonymous and semi-anonymous testimony into named, identifiable former officers speaking on camera, with signed affidavits archived and published in facsimile. The affidavit set on Hastings's own document archive names Robert Salas, Charles Halt, Patrick McDonough, Robert Jamison, Dwynne Arneson, Bruce Fenstermacher and Jerry Nelson - seven witnesses, matching the seven veterans described as speaking. Hastings told the room that 'whoever are aboard this craft are sending a signal to both Washington and Moscow, among others, that we are playing with fire', and that the possession and threatened use of nuclear weapons 'threatens the human race and the integrity of the planetary environment'. The speakers urged the US government to reveal the facts. The evidentiary claim here is narrow and should stay narrow: what the event establishes is not that craft disabled missiles, but that a group of named commissioned and non-commissioned officers were willing to say under their own names, in a venue with legal consequences for defamation and with signed affidavits on file, that these incidents occurred.

dossier.narrative:
The event is well documented: a named venue, a fixed date, a roster with ranks, units and periods, and live national coverage. As an artefact it is exactly what this board wants, and the claims on this node are Tier 2 for the fact that these men said these things on that date.

The provenance underneath is where the care goes, and the node records it rather than leaving a reader to assume seven independent voices. Of the seven, one had already written the operative document himself as a serving deputy base commander in 1981, which is a materially different position from recounting a memory decades later. Another had published independently. The remainder reached the public through the organiser's interview programme.

This node also carries a data-integrity flag rather than a quiet correction. The fetch of the organiser's own roster page by this session rendered one veteran's incident year differently from every other source opened, including that veteran's own testimony elsewhere. The board records the discrepancy and does not silently pick the version it prefers.

And it records that the organiser's own pages give two different totals for how many veterans he has interviewed, 150 on one and more than 160 on another, with no statement anywhere of how they were recruited. That absence is the largest unanswered provenance question in the cluster. It is not an accusation. It is a gap that only he can close, and the board notes it in the same tone it would note a missing service record.
openQuestions: The organiser's recruitment method, stated nowhere on his own pages.
A complete recording or transcript of the 27 September 2010 panel, as opposed to coverage of it.
Which of the seven, if any, had made a public statement before being contacted.
dossier.whatItIs: The UFO-Nukes Connection press conference at the National Press Club, Washington DC, on 27 September 2010, at which seven named USAF veterans spoke on the record about incursions at nuclear weapons sites. CNN streamed it live and carried coverage. It was organised by Robert Hastings.
dossier.whyImplicated: It is the single dated artefact through which most of this cluster's testimony entered public life at once, which makes it both the cluster's most useful anchor and the place its provenance question is sharpest. Seven men, one organiser, one day. Understanding how each of them got onto that panel is the difference between seven independent accounts and one collection.
